description: The most relevant number of the problem "global warming" of the start page ranking and the potential solution: without a border adjustment a large share of the emissions avoided in a regulated region reappears in a region without a carbon price. The carbon leakage rate with and without a border adjustment and the coverage of the global emissions by a direct carbon price are the figures that decide whether a unilateral climate policy is effective at all.

words.name: reduction
words.description: the gain of electrons by a species during a reaction

words.name: price
words.description: amount of money required to buy something
Calendar year 2019, reference year for the emission baseline.

words.name: solution
words.description: a homogeneous mixture of a solute dissolved in a solvent

words.name: afforestation
words.description: Afforestation and reforestation as carbon sinks. Wide IPCC range; permanence, land competition and fire risk limit reliability. Translation of the German keyword 'Aufforstung'.

words.name: hydropower
words.description: Expansion and modernization of hydroelectric generation, limited by sites, ecology and drought risk. Translation of the German keyword 'Wasserkraft'.

words.name: electrification
words.description: Switching industrial processes, transport and heat from fossil fuels to clean electricity. Translation of the German keyword 'Elektrifizierung'.

words.name: cycling
words.description: Shift of short trips to bikes and e-bikes via safe infrastructure. Small global potential but very cheap per tonne. Translation of the German keyword 'Radverkehr'.

words.name: sufficiency
words.description: Demand reduction through changed consumption patterns: smaller living space, less driving and flying, longer product use. Cheap in money, hard socially. Translation of the German keyword 'Suffizienz'.

words.name: research
words.description: systematic investigation to discover new knowledge

words.name: innovation
words.description: Commercialization, scale-up and learning-curve effects turning research into deployed technology. Overlaps with research. Translation of the German keyword 'Innovation'.

words.name: digitalization
words.description: Smart grids, building automation and logistics optimization, net of rebound and data-center growth. Translation of the German keyword 'Digitalisierung'.

triples.name: reduce climate gas emissions
triples.description: a transparent, publicly calculated climate tariff that prices the emissions of imports and exports and thereby stops carbon leakage (concept paper section 3)

triples.name: carbon leakage
triples.description: the share of the emissions avoided in a regulated region that reappears in a region with little or no carbon price

triples.name: carbon tariff
triples.description: a carbon border adjustment mechanism that puts imports on the same carbon price footing as domestic production

triples.name: probability range factor
triples.description: the number that the centre of an estimate is multiplied by to get one bound of its probability range; each bound has its own factor, because a range can be asymmetric, e.g. if one side is limited by a zero level

triples.name: reduction potential
triples.description: Criterion: additional greenhouse gas reduction a solution can deliver globally per year by about 2035 versus a current-policy baseline. Unit: Gt CO2eq per year. Range given as minimum and maximum spans about one standard deviation around the central estimate.

triples.name: fulfillment probability
triples.description: Criterion: probability that the reduction potential is actually delivered once the initial setup is done, reflecting political, social and technical execution risk. Dimensionless, 0 to 1. Range spans about one standard deviation.

triples.name: greenhouse gas emission
triples.description: Release of a greenhouse gas into the atmosphere.

triples.name: global greenhouse gas emissions
triples.description: Global net anthropogenic greenhouse gas emissions in Gt CO2eq per year.

triples.name: border tariff
triples.description: A duty levied on goods when they cross a customs border.

triples.name: carbon border tariff
triples.description: Carbon border adjustment (CBAM-type) extending carbon pricing to imports and reducing leakage; EU CBAM operational since 2026. Translation of the German keyword 'Klimazoll'.

triples.name: climate solution
triples.description: A mitigation option that reduces global greenhouse gas emissions, ranked here by effort return score.

triples.name: solar energy
triples.description: Utility-scale and rooftop photovoltaics. Largest and cheapest 2030 potential in IPCC AR6 Figure SPM.7; deployment already on a steep growth track. Translation of the German keyword 'Solarenergie'.

triples.name: wind energy
triples.description: Onshore and offshore wind power. Second largest low-cost 2030 potential in IPCC AR6 Figure SPM.7. Translation of the German keyword 'Windenergie'.

triples.name: nuclear energy
triples.description: New nuclear plants and lifetime extensions. Low-carbon but slow to build; near-term potential limited by construction times. Translation of the German keyword 'Kernenergie'.

triples.name: methane reduction
triples.description: Cutting CH4 from oil, gas, coal, waste and agriculture. UNEP/CCAC: up to 45 percent (180 Mt CH4/yr, about 5 Gt CO2eq at GWP100) by 2030, avoiding about 0.3 degree C by the 2040s; majority of measures at low or negative cost. Translation of the German keyword 'Methanreduktion'.

triples.name: coal phase-out
triples.description: Replacing coal-fired power and heat with low-carbon generation. Largest single fossil emission source. Overlaps strongly with solar energy and wind energy; potentials must not be summed. Translation of the German keyword 'Kohleausstieg'.

triples.name: energy efficiency
triples.description: Cross-sector efficiency in industry, buildings, appliances and processes. IEA calls it the first fuel; most measures have negative lifetime cost. Translation of the German keyword 'Energieeffizienz'.

triples.name: building renovation
triples.description: Deep energy retrofits of the existing building stock (insulation, windows, heating systems). High potential but chronically low renovation rates. Translation of the German keyword 'Gebäudesanierung'.

triples.name: heat pumps
triples.description: Replacing fossil heating boilers with electric heat pumps in buildings and low-temperature industry. Translation of the German keyword 'Wärmepumpen'.

triples.name: district heating
triples.description: Decarbonized heat networks using waste heat, large heat pumps, geothermal and thermal storage in dense areas. Translation of the German keyword 'Fernwärme'.

triples.name: geothermal energy
triples.description: Geothermal electricity and direct heat use, including emerging deep and enhanced systems. Translation of the German keyword 'Geothermie'.

triples.name: energy storage
triples.description: Batteries, pumped hydro and long-duration storage. Enabler that unlocks variable renewables rather than a direct emission cut; potential counted as enabled reduction. Translation of the German keyword 'Energiespeicher'.

triples.name: grid expansion
triples.description: Transmission and distribution build-out plus interconnectors. Enabler for renewables integration; potential counted as enabled reduction. Translation of the German keyword 'Netzausbau'.

triples.name: speed limit
triples.description: General motorway speed limits. Tiny global potential (Germany alone below 0.01 Gt/yr) but near-zero setup cost. Translation of the German keyword 'Tempolimit'.

triples.name: climate dividend
triples.description: Per-capita refund of carbon price revenue. Direct effect small; main value is raising public acceptance and thus the fulfillment probability of carbon pricing. Translation of the German keyword 'Klimageld'.

triples.name: emissions trading
triples.description: Cap-and-trade systems with declining caps (EU ETS and successors). Overlaps with carbon price; proven instrument. Translation of the German keyword 'Emissionshandel'.

triples.name: electric mobility
triples.description: Battery-electric passenger vehicles plus charging infrastructure. Strong market momentum. Translation of the German keyword 'Elektromobilität'.

triples.name: freight transport
triples.description: Electric and efficient trucks, rail modal shift and logistics optimization for goods transport. Translation of the German keyword 'Güterverkehr'.

triples.name: circular economy
triples.description: System-wide reuse, remanufacturing and product life extension reducing primary material demand. Overlaps with recycling and material efficiency. Translation of the German keyword 'Kreislaufwirtschaft'.

triples.name: material efficiency
triples.description: Lightweight design, higher material yields and substitution (e.g. low-clinker cement, timber construction). Translation of the German keyword 'Materialeffizienz'.

triples.name: peatland rewetting
triples.description: Rewetting drained peatlands, which currently emit on the order of 1 to 2 Gt CO2eq/yr globally. Translation of the German keyword 'Wiedervernässung'.

triples.name: soil carbon
triples.description: Organic carbon stored in the soil.

triples.name: soil carbon buildup
triples.description: Soil carbon sequestration on cropland and grassland (cover crops, agroforestry, improved grazing). Measurement and permanence remain difficult. Translation of the German keyword 'Humusaufbau'.

triples.name: carbon capture
triples.description: Separating CO2 from a gas stream so that it can be stored or used.

triples.name: carbon capture and storage
triples.description: Capturing CO2 at industrial point sources and storing it geologically. Historically weak delivery record; costly per tonne. Translation of the German keyword 'CCS'.

triples.name: carbon capture and utilization
triples.description: Using captured CO2 in fuels and materials. Small net potential because most uses re-release CO2 and demand large clean energy input. Translation of the German keyword 'CCU'.

triples.name: green hydrogen
triples.description: Electrolytic hydrogen for steel, chemicals, shipping and long-term storage. Limited to hard-to-electrify uses; expectations corrected downward since 2023. Translation of the German keyword 'Grüner Wasserstoff'.

triples.name: sustainable agriculture
triples.description: Improved nutrient management, rice cultivation, livestock feeding and manure handling reducing N2O and CH4. Translation of the German keyword 'Nachhaltige Landwirtschaft'.

triples.name: meat consumption
triples.description: The amount of meat eaten.

triples.name: reduced meat consumption
triples.description: Shift toward plant-rich diets. IPCC sustainable healthy diets potential includes freed agricultural land; very cheap in money, slow in behavior. Translation of the German keyword 'Weniger Fleisch'.

triples.name: food waste
triples.description: Food that is lost or thrown away along the supply chain.

triples.name: food waste reduction
triples.description: Cutting food loss and waste along the whole chain, reducing agricultural production needs. Translation of the German keyword 'Lebensmittelverschwendung'.

triples.name: aviation emission
triples.description: Greenhouse gas released by air traffic.

triples.name: aviation emission reduction
triples.description: Sustainable aviation fuels, efficiency and demand management for the roughly 1 Gt CO2/yr aviation sector. Translation of the German keyword 'Flugverkehr'.

triples.name: emission standards
triples.description: Binding CO2 and efficiency standards for vehicles, appliances and buildings. Regulation is cheap to set up and has a strong track record. Translation of the German keyword 'CO₂-Standards'.

triples.name: climate finance
triples.description: Concessional finance and de-risking for mitigation in developing countries; enabler whose potential is the reduction it unlocks. Translation of the German keyword 'Klimafinanzierung'.

triples.name: supply chain
triples.description: The chain of suppliers that contribute to a final product.

triples.name: supply chain laws
triples.description: Due diligence and disclosure duties pushing emission cuts through corporate supply chains. Translation of the German keyword 'Lieferkettengesetze'.

triples.name: fossil subsidy
triples.description: Public financial support that lowers the price of fossil fuels.

triples.name: fossil subsidy removal
triples.description: Removing explicit fossil fuel subsidies (IMF: 725 billion USD in 2024; removal cuts CO2 about 6 percent below baseline by 2035). Saves public money; politically explosive. Translation of the German keyword 'Subventionsabbau'.

triples.name: international agreements
triples.description: Treaties and pledges (Paris Agreement, Global Methane Pledge, CBAM clubs) that coordinate national action; potential counted as enabled reduction. Translation of the German keyword 'Internationale Abkommen'.

formulas.name: global happy time points
formulas.description: convert a share of the global welfare given in percent into happy time points by multiplying it with the number of humans on earth, so that a percent loss or gain can be compared with absolute welfare numbers

formulas.name: avoided potential loss
formulas.description: the reward of a solution in trillion EUR, the potential loss of the problem multiplied by the share of the loss that the solution is expected to avoid

formulas.name: reward ratio (formula)
formulas.description: the avoided loss per person year of effort, the potential loss multiplied by the expected loss reduction and divided by the effort needed, to rank the solutions by their leverage
formulas.expression: "reward ratio","trillion","EUR per person year" = "potential","loss","trillion","EUR" * "loss reduction","percent" / "initial effort","person year"

formulas.name: probability range low
formulas.description: the lower bound of the probability range of an estimate, the estimate multiplied by its low range factor; the centre is the stated target value and each bound is calculated on its own, so that a range can be asymmetric

formulas.name: probability range high
formulas.description: the upper bound of the probability range of an estimate, the estimate multiplied by its high range factor; the centre is the stated target value and each bound is calculated on its own, so that a range can be asymmetric

formulas.name: annual damage in money
formulas.description: the loss that a problem causes each year in money, the world GDP multiplied by the share of it that the problem costs per year

formulas.name: loss reduction by a carbon tariff
formulas.description: the share of the potential loss that the emission reduction avoids, the share of the emissions that the carbon tariff keeps from leaking into a region without a carbon price; the leakage rate change is negative, because it is a reduction, while the avoided share of the loss is stated positive

formulas.name: long run damage share of the GDP
formulas.description: the share of the world GDP that a problem costs at the end of its development, the share it costs today multiplied by the factor by which the damage still grows; the share is stated negative, because it is a loss

formulas.name: welfare damage share
formulas.description: the share of the global happy time points that a problem costs, the share of the GDP it costs multiplied by the factor by which the welfare damage exceeds the money damage, because htp counts the healthy life years that the GDP does not (concept paper introduction)

formulas.name: initial effort of a solution
formulas.description: the person years needed to set up a solution, the annual damage of the problem in money multiplied by the effort needed per trillion EUR of damage

formulas.name: avoided welfare loss
formulas.description: the happy time points that a solution saves, the world happy time points multiplied by the share of them that the problem costs and by the share of that loss which the solution avoids; the result is stated positive, because it is a gain

formulas.name: loss reduction by a climate solution
formulas.description: the share of the potential loss of the warming that a climate solution avoids, the expected emission reduction of the solution, the middle of its reduction potential range times the middle of its fulfillment probability range, divided by the global greenhouse gas emissions
formulas.expression: "loss reduction","percent" = ( "reduction potential","minimum" + "reduction potential","maximum" ) / 2 * ( "fulfillment probability","minimum" + "fulfillment probability","maximum" ) / 2 / "global greenhouse gas emissions","2019"

formulas.name: loss reduction by a climate solution low
formulas.description: the lower bound of the loss reduction of a climate solution, the minimum reduction potential times the minimum fulfillment probability divided by the global greenhouse gas emissions
formulas.expression: "loss reduction","percent" = "reduction potential","minimum" * "fulfillment probability","minimum" / "global greenhouse gas emissions","2019"

formulas.name: loss reduction by a climate solution high
formulas.description: the upper bound of the loss reduction of a climate solution, the maximum reduction potential times the maximum fulfillment probability divided by the global greenhouse gas emissions
formulas.expression: "loss reduction","percent" = "reduction potential","maximum" * "fulfillment probability","maximum" / "global greenhouse gas emissions","2019"

formulas.name: person years per billion USD by the carbon border tariff
formulas.description: the conversion of an initial effort in billion USD into person years, calibrated on the carbon border tariff, whose effort in person years is the initial effort of the solution reduce climate gas emissions and whose effort in billion USD is the middle of its range in co2_eq_reduction_ranking.json

formulas.name: initial effort of a climate solution
formulas.description: the person years needed to set up a climate solution, the middle of its initial effort range in billion USD times the person years per billion USD

formulas.name: initial effort of a climate solution low
formulas.description: the lower bound of the initial effort of a climate solution, the minimum initial effort in billion USD times the person years per billion USD

formulas.name: initial effort of a climate solution high
formulas.description: the upper bound of the initial effort of a climate solution, the maximum initial effort in billion USD times the person years per billion USD
